mario.title: Super Mario Bros. NES
mario.observation: World 1-1 shows short obstacle jumps and higher jumps at blocks and stairs. Pixel aspect and capture frame remain intact; the footage exposes motion, not button state.
mario.recorderCredit: Gameplay Project · YouTube Creative Commons Attribution

metroid.title: Metroid Dread · Kraid, phase 2
metroid.observation: Ground-level shots hit the lower weak point; Samus moves up to the magnetic platform and lines up shots at Kraid's head. Shows the reason to choose a height. Dread's movement timings are not treated as measurements of the NES game.

ghosts.title: Ghosts 'n Goblins Resurrection
ghosts.observation: The branch-platform and water crossing excerpts visibly show committed lateral jump arcs. Segment-level points will exclude promotional title cards and use only the illustrated movement, as distinct from a long uninterrupted player recording. Keep the existing game composition and release marks.
ghosts.recorderCredit: Capcom France · YouTube Creative Commons Attribution

smash.title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate
smash.observation: Earlier match sequence from the old jump-physics audit, at native speed. Show visible ground and airborne states; own diagram shows the separate input timing rather than attributing telemetry to the recording.

exactOriginalMetroid.decision: Keep the slower original movement as an independently authored comparison. Move the visible aiming-height role to Dread's separately verified gameplay.

streetFighter2Piledriver.decision: The old project labeled this an excerpt and documented the technique. Recorder reuse is not established for the new version. Use the separate Capcom France Street Fighter 6 training view for the move, then compare timings on a clearly labeled schematic.

zangief.title: Street Fighter 6 · Zangief, Screw Piledriver
zangief.observation: Local 7.7–16.7 shows the grab, camera rising to reveal the spin, and the impact on the floor. This is the modern move. It is not frame evidence for Hyper Fighting timing.
zangief.recorderCredit: Capcom France · YouTube Creative Commons Attribution

celeste.title: Celeste · the first chapter
celeste.observation: The chapter one room around 80–99 seconds shows changes in horizontal position and turns close to walls while airborne. This is a different native segment from DS02's prologue and bridge shots.
